models_evaluated: 13 renal cell carcinoma classification deep-learning models

links.outcome: Operational greenhouse-gas emissions from digital pathology deep learning
links.effect: Worldwide yearly emissions reached up to 16 Mt (95% CI 6·8–37·6), requiring up to 86 590 km2 (0·22%) of forest.
links.quote: Yearly CO 2 eq emissions varied based on the various parameters, reaching up to 16 megatons (Mt; 95% CI 6·8–37·6) of CO 2 eq, requiring up to 86 590 km 2 (36 476–200 796; 0·22%, 0·09–0·51) of the world's forest to sequester the emissions ( figure 3C, D ).

links.effect: VGG16 outperformed ConvNeXt while reducing CO2eq emissions by approximately 8 times.
links.quote: Despite having fewer trainable parameters, VGG16, a relatively simple deep-learning model, outperformed ConvNeXt, a deeper model, while reducing CO 2 eq emissions by approximately 8 times ( figure 4A ; appendix pp 21–22 ).

unlisted_practices: Using tissue-only or ROI-only input tiles instead of entire whole-slide images to reduce CO2eq emissions
Pruning deep-learning models to reduce emissions while retaining accuracy
Using pathomics as an alternative histopathology analysis approach to reduce emissions
Selecting small or computationally less demanding models for digital pathology
Considering renewable-energy sources and efficient hardware for AI computation

links.outcome: annual operational CO2 equivalent emissions of digital pathology deep learning
links.effect: Applying large models to all WSI tiles of prostate and breast cases resulted in yearly CO2 eq emissions of 7·65 t (95% CI 7·62–7·68) for 1-task up to 100·56 t (100·21–100·99) for 7-tasks.
links.quote: Applying large deep-learning models on all WSI tiles of prostate and breast pathology cases would result in yearly CO 2 eq emissions of 7·65 tons (t; 95% CI 7·62–7·68) in the 1-task scenario; yearly CO 2 eq emissions were up to 100·56 t (100·21–100·99) in the 7-task scenario ( figure 2A ).

unlisted_practices: Input data reduction by analyzing only tissue-containing or region-of-interest tiles rather than entire whole-slide images to reduce operational emissions
Model pruning to reduce operational energy consumption and greenhouse-gas emissions while retaining diagnostic accuracy
Using pathomics (morphological feature extraction) instead of deep learning to reduce operational emissions
